name: PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk

frontmatter.title: IMJS: a car-rental and financing book inside the Indomobil holding, priced near its parts
frontmatter.summary: Indomobil Multi Jasa holds a vehicle-rental fleet and a consumer-financing book under a family-controlled listed parent. The finance book is marked at its disclosed fair value, the other parts at carrying value, and a governance-only holding-company discount is applied. The parts sit close to the price, no dated catalyst narrows the discount, and the earnings cross-check runs from far below the parts to about the price; the call is HOLD on either anchor.
thesis: The parts are worth modestly more than the price once honestly marked: the financing book at the fair value the notes disclose, the fleet and smaller balances at carrying value, the group residual net assets included rather than dropped, and a mechanical roll on top.

The discount does the work, not a re-rating: we apply the wide end of the shares' own four observable price-to-book years as a governance and upstream discount, benchmarked to the house base-rate card, and credit no narrowing because no dated action forces one.

The earnings leg is struck on the audited group result, the basis on which the group bears the loss-making subsidiaries' losses, with the minority allocation nil forward; that audited year is a trough, and the last-twelve-month bridge is published as the upside anchor.

The book-multiple leg is removed rather than carried: a justified price-to-book at an audited return on equity of 0.4% against a cost of equity above twenty per cent is negative, so the own-history book multiple has no supportable value.

What would change the view: a dated event that upstreams value to minority holders — a tender, a buyback, a structural rise in the dividend or an asset sale — a placement or controller sell-down that closes the free-float gap, or a credit deterioration the fair-value mark has not captured.

catalysts.event: IMJS sets up PT Indomobil Global Ventura, a financing and venture-capital subsidiary, describing itself as a holding company
Deadline for the third-quarter interim report, the first hard test of whether the first half earnings recovery persists
Annual general meeting for the 2026 financial year, with the dividend decision and the next capital-allocation call
Regulatory deadline to lift the free float from the reported level to the exchange minimum, which can only be met by a controller sell-down or new shares

blocks.text: We rate PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk **HOLD** with a twelve-month target of Rp138 against a price of Rp150, a total return of -8.0%. The company is the listed rental and financing arm of the Indomobil group: two operating books it controls almost entirely, on one leveraged balance sheet, under a parent that holds almost all of the shares [S3], [S8].

This revision arguments the earnings-leg anchor and publishes the last-twelve-month bridge in section four, on the group basis the accepted correction requires [S3], [S2]. The marginal funding rate is labelled as the red team's assumption rather than a disclosed coupon, and only new money pays it, so the base case stays profitable [S3], [S2].

The sum of the parts — the financing book at its disclosed fair value, the fleet and smaller balances at carrying value, the residual net assets, less look-through net funding and the minority's claim at the audited date, then discounted — is Rp160 [S3]. That is above the price, but the earnings cross-check is Rp27 at the own-history multiple, and the two-leg blend lands below the price before the roll [S0], [S3]. The book-multiple leg stays removed: a justified price-to-book at an audited return on equity of 0.4% against a cost of equity of 21.2% is negative [S0], [S3].

The anchor year is the whole argument. The audited group result, 19.2 IDR bn, is the trough of a collapse the first half has already reversed: profit to the parent in the first half, 170 IDR bn, exceeds the whole audited parent year, 123 IDR bn [S2], [S3]. The last-twelve-month group result is therefore a multiple of the audited year; section four publishes its components and what it does to the target. On that anchor the target sits at the top of the HOLD band, on the audited anchor below the price — both HOLD, and we publish the lower rather than pick the flattering one.

We credit no narrowing of the discount: no dated action forces one, and the card's route for a below-parts price without a named catalyst is the event-driven book or a pass. The one dated event — the free-float deadline — widens rather than narrows the gap. Two boundaries: the marks are sourced balance-sheet values, not segment appraisals; and the minority allocation is nil forward, with the audited split disclosed [S3], [S0].

A lender's losses arrive a year or two after the underwriting decision that created them, which is why a
valuation like this one leans on the carrying value of the loan book and the provisions against it rather
than on the current run rate of profit.

PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk reports two segments close to halves of the revenue line: car rental and related, which earned 3,529 IDR bn in the audited year, and financial services, which earned 2,256 IDR bn [S3]. The split is roughly three-fifths rental and two-fifths financing on the company's own segment review [S3]. The group employs 2,800.0 people and is headquartered at the Indomobil Tower in East Jakarta [S0], [S3].

The rental segment runs through PT CSM Corporatama and its subsidiaries, principally the trucking arm PT Indomobil Bussan Trucking, and sells more than a fleet on hire: logistics and transportation, workshop and driver services, and training through PT Indomobil Edukasi Utama [S6]. Its customers are weighted to corporates, so revenue is contracted and the cost base is fleet depreciation [S2], [S3].

The financing segment is the consumer side: PT Indomobil Finance Indonesia, held at almost the whole of its equity, writes consumer financing, finance lease and factoring against motorcycles, cars new and used, commercial vehicles and heavy equipment [S3]. It funds itself in the bank and bond market and is regulated as a multifinance company; it is where the group leverage lives [S3].

Control is concentrated and the chain is short. PT Indomobil Sukses Internasional Tbk holds the overwhelming majority of IMJS, which owns almost all of the financing and rental subsidiaries; the ultimate parent is Gallant Venture Ltd, a Singapore-listed investment holding company through which the controlling family interest runs [S3], [S8]. In the closing weeks of 2025 IMJS completed its fourth pre-emptive rights issue, lifting the issued capital to 10,849,262,500 shares, and paid the entire net proceeds of 499 IDR bn into the rental subsidiary [S3]. In September 2026 the group set up PT Indomobil Global Ventura for financing and venture-capital activity, describing IMJS as a holding company [S7].
Reading a group like this is mostly a question of following the cash rather than the org chart.

Both businesses sit downstream of Indonesia's vehicle cycle, and that cycle turned in the current year. National car wholesales were 804,195 units in the audited year, down roughly seven per cent as purchasing power weakened, credit tightened and the policy rate fell more slowly than lending rates [S3]. The current year is different: nine-month wholesales reached 679,020 units, up about a fifth, and motorcycles grew only marginally, so this is a car-market recovery rather than a broad one [S9], [S3].

The multifinance pool is large, slow and well regulated. Industry receivables were 506,500 IDR bn at the end of the audited year, growing by less than a percentage point, with gross non-performing financing of 2.5% and group gearing a little over two times [S3]. With the pool growing that slowly and credit costs under three per cent, the competitive variables are funding cost and distribution reach, not credit appetite.

The house backdrop is not a tailwind. The regime is balance-of-payments pressure with a cautious stance and an explicit AVOID tilt on rate-sensitive consumer-discretionary and net-interest-margin names, which is what a leveraged auto-financing and rental book is; the deck holds the policy rate at 5.8% and takes the rupiah to Rp18,350/USD per dollar from a spot of Rp18,025/USD [S0]. We credit no rate relief: revenue compounds on the company's run rate and the deck's nominal path, and gross margin is held at the level delivered [S0], [S2], [S3].

IMJS is a challenger in both markets. Its financing book of 16,664 IDR bn is a fraction of the industry total, and its fleet of 11,080 IDR bn makes it a mid-sized lessor crowded by the captive arms of the distribution groups and the banks' leasing subsidiaries [S3]. Its edge is the distribution group: it writes paper against vehicles its shareholders distribute and service, with joint-financing arrangements that share funding and, where recourse applies, credit risk [S3]. The moat is that network, not any structural advantage in leasing: rental economics turn on residual values and utilisation, and a group that both distributes and services the marques has an edge a standalone lessor lacks [S6]. Buyer power is high because fleets can be tendered; supplier power is meaningful; substitution from short-term hire is real and rivalry intense. The one helpful force is entry: capital and the multifinance licence keep the smallest competitors out [S3].

**The history is steady revenue and collapsing returns.** Revenue rose from 4,825.4 to 5,785.2 over the four audited years at a mid-single-digit rate, and gross margin held a narrow band, ending at 37.9% [S0], [S3]. Almost none reached the bottom: group profit fell from 269.6 to 19.2 across the two most recent audited years, and return on equity slid to 0.4% [S0], [S3]. The reason is arithmetic: debt of 26,569.5 against equity of 5,001.6, and finance charges of 880 IDR bn against operating income of 970 IDR bn, left pre-tax profit a small fraction of gross profit [S3]. The company is in substance a spread business that paid a larger margin on its liabilities than it earned on its assets.

**Restating depreciation is the most important correction in this file.** The data pack carries only the slice of depreciation sitting in administrative expenses; the audited note shows the true charge at 915 IDR bn, with 809 IDR bn the year before and 734 IDR bn before that [S3], [S4]. That is roughly ten times the pack's figure, and it turns the apparent profitability around: the correct reading is an EBITDA margin of 32.6%. We restate depreciation, operating income and pre-tax profit from the filing, because the pack's pre-tax line is struck before the final tax [S3].

**The first half is the turn, and it is real.** Revenue of 3,311 IDR bn in the six months to June, with operating income of 600 IDR bn and depreciation of 541 IDR bn, implies a mid-thirties EBITDA margin on revenue up roughly a fifth [S2]. Profit to the parent of 170 IDR bn already exceeds the whole audited parent year [S2], [S3]. The last-twelve-month bridge stated once: the audited group total 19.2 IDR bn plus the current first half 120 IDR bn less the prior-year first half 49.8 IDR bn [S3], [S2].

**Cash flow and earnings quality.** The audited year's operating cash flow was negative, -59.0 IDR bn, against restated EBITDA an order of magnitude larger, so the group funded itself from the balance sheet [S3]. That is the card's first flag, and it reverses in the current year: the first half produced 1,129 IDR bn of operating cash flow against a negative prior-year half, and the prior audited year 2,217 IDR bn [S2], [S3]. The pattern is a deterioration reversed, not earnings outrunning cash, so we read the audited outflow as the working capital of a growing receivable book. Related-party balances are disclosed in both directions, with trade receivables of 146 IDR bn and payables of 178 IDR bn against revenue of 5,785.2 [S3]. We found no pledge of the controlling stake, no special-monitoring or special-notation status, and an unmodified audit opinion [S3].

**Funding cost.** Our forecast keeps the fleet structure — capex at the audited ratio, working capital growing with the book, and borrowing priced on a split basis: the held stock of 26,569.5 at its realised rate, only incremental debt at the marginal price the red team accepted, an all-in 3.74% on opening debt [S3], [S2], [S0]. The marginal rate is an assumption, not a disclosed coupon: the filing shows facility sizes but no rate, while the audited 880 IDR bn of finance charges is what the existing book pays [S3], [S2]. Interest rises from 993.7 to 2,127.8, against 880.2 audited, with later years understating the marginal charge because the engine carries one scalar. Dividends are a token: the board declared 3.8 IDR bn, and we hold the per-share amount rather than a payout ratio [S8].

The house method for a holding company is a sum of the parts. We mark the finance book at the fair value the notes disclose, the fleet and the two smaller balances at carrying value, include the residual net assets, deduct the look-through net funding and the minority's book claim at the same audited date, and apply a governance-only discount [S3]. No segment multiple is applied because the company publishes no segment balance sheet or segment profit below the gross profit line.

The bridge reconciles to the accounts. The four marked balances — finance book at carrying value 16,664 IDR bn, fleet 11,080 IDR bn, investment property 770 IDR bn, investment in shares 624 IDR bn — plus the residual (total assets 32,902 IDR bn less those marks and cash 2,077 IDR bn, against total liabilities 27,808 IDR bn less debt 26,570 IDR bn) give gross parts equal to parent book equity of 5,002 IDR bn plus net funding 24,492.1 and the minority claim 91.9 IDR bn [S3]. Re-marking the finance book to its disclosed fair value of 15,995 IDR bn gives net asset value, and after the discount the sum of the parts is Rp160.

| Component | Mark | Value | Source | |---|---|---|---| | Financial services — financing receivables (PT Indomobil Finance Indonesia) | disclosed fair value | 15,995 IDR bn | [S3] | | Car rental and related — net fixed assets (PT CSM Corporatama and related) | carrying value | 11,080 IDR bn | [S3] | | Investment property, net | carrying value | 770 IDR bn | [S3] | | Investment in shares (associates and unlisted stakes) | carrying value | 624 IDR bn | [S3] | | Other net assets and liabilities | residual of the statement (32,902 IDR bn less the marks and 2,077 IDR bn; less 27,808 IDR bn net of 26,570 IDR bn) | see bridge | [S3] | | Group net debt, audited 31 December 2025 | audited balance sheet | 24,492.1 | [S3] | | Non-controlling interests' book claim, same date | audited balance sheet | 91.9 IDR bn | [S3] | | Sum of the parts, after the holding-company discount | primary method | Rp160 | [S3] |

The audited marks are not a floor. Against the interim balance sheet the marked parts rise — fleet 11,538 IDR bn, investment property 778 IDR bn, investment in shares 655 IDR bn, receivables 9,187 IDR bn — but so do matching liabilities: debt 26,949 IDR bn against 26,570 IDR bn, cash 1,552 IDR bn against 2,077 IDR bn, minority claim 43.3 IDR bn against 91.9 IDR bn [S3], [S2]. The matched re-mark lowers net asset value, and we disclose it rather than re-mark one side.

**The earnings leg and the anchor year.** The P/E multiple is the mean of the shares' four observable own-history observations, struck on parent earnings; applied to the audited group result of 19.2 IDR bn it gives Rp27, -83.3% below the parts [S0], [S3]. That audited year is a trough, and this report does not hide it. The last-twelve-month bridge above — 19.2 IDR bn plus 120 IDR bn less 49.8 IDR bn — is the current earnings level: on it the same 15.1 times multiple gives a leg several times the carried Rp27, lifts the static blend to roughly the price, and after the roll and the haircut puts the target at the top of the HOLD band [S3], [S2], [S0]. The rating is HOLD on either anchor, and the published target is the lower of the two. The reason is plain: the model binds the leg to the last audited actual, so striking it on the last-twelve-month result would mean restating an audited year or rewriting the data pack, and this desk permits neither. The published target is therefore the floor of the range, not its midpoint.

The book multiple is removed and zero-weighted: its own-history multiple was struck on book earning 0.4% against a cost of equity of 21.2%, and the justified price-to-book at that return is negative [S0], [S3]. The engine renormalises the remaining two legs, so the blend lands at Rp126 before the roll and the haircut.

The rupiah risk-free rate, the Indonesian default spread, an equity risk premium and a country premium give a cost of equity of 21.2% on an unlevered beta at the industry default, levered by a debt-to-capitalisation input of 2.00 [S0]; the input is the default because the financing book's funding would otherwise drive the levered beta beyond a usable range. Because the target is rolled forward at the cost of equity, a higher rate raises the target — the rate is not the conservative part of this valuation, the discount is. The block prices new debt at 9.4% while the P&L pays a blended 3.74%; the weighted average cost of capital is 12.0%.

The sensitivity grid runs the discount against the cost of equity, and value is far more sensitive to the discount. What discount would make the shares fairly valued on our marks? 62% — the market prices the parts at a wider discount than we apply [S3]. That is not a call to buy. The expected return is the mechanical cost-of-equity roll on static marks, not a view that the discount narrows: without the roll the blend is Rp126 against the price [S0]. With no named and dated catalyst, the card sends a below-parts price to the event-driven book or to a pass, and on the house's own terms the rating is HOLD.
The risks are financial rather than operational.

**Credit cost in the financing book — likelihood moderate, impact high.** The auditor's key audit matter is the allowance for impairment on consumer financing and finance lease receivables [S2]. The book is marked at fair value 15,995 IDR bn against carrying value 16,664 IDR bn, so deterioration must exhaust the 426 IDR bn non-current allowance and the mark already taken before it reaches our value; even so, a few points of extra loss would remove most of the group profit at this leverage [S3], [S2]. The shock grammar cannot re-mark a holding, so the credit channel is carried in the bear's margin shock and disclosed here.

**Funding cost and refinancing — likelihood moderate, impact high.** The group is a spread business funded in the bank and bond market, and its own review complains that lending rates fell more slowly than the policy rate [S3]. The forecast holds the legacy stock at its realised rate and prices only new money at the assumed marginal rate; if the legacy book repriced faster, interest would run above the model — an asymmetry disclosed rather than smoothed.

**Governance and control — likelihood high, impact moderate.** The parent holds nearly all of the shares, the float is small, and the company has raised equity four times, most recently in late 2025 at a price well above today's [S3], [S8]. Related-party balances in both directions are material [S3].

**Liquidity and the free-float deadline — likelihood high, impact moderate.** The name fails the investability gate: the float is 8.0% with the parent holding 92.0%, and three-month average daily traded value is 925,233,352.4, hence the 10% haircut [S0]. The float is also a dated supply event: the minimum free float is 15.0% by 31 March 2029, and IMJS is well short [S10]. The gap can only close through a controller sell-down or new shares, either of which can dilute or overhang the minority.

**Cycle, regulation and currency — likelihood moderate, impact moderate.** A vehicle-market relapse would slow both books [S9], and multifinance capital and gearing rules are tightening [S3]. Dollar funding sits on both segments — a 350 USD mn facility at the financing subsidiary and a 190 USD mn one at the rental subsidiary — while hedging receivables are small and the cash-flow-hedge reserve stood at -235 IDR bn [S3]. The deck carries the rupiah to Rp18,350/USD against spot of Rp18,025/USD, and a move beyond that would run through that reserve, the book value this valuation leans on [S0], [S3].

**Scenarios.** The discount is the dominant lever: the bear carries it to the widest of the shares' own four observable years, the bull narrows it, and each case carries a mirrored revenue shock of three percentage points and a mirrored gross-margin shock of two points, the margin shock being the operating channel through which credit cost reaches the forecast [S2], [S3]. That shock moves the forecast but not the two valuation legs, which are struck on the audited balance sheet or the multiple history; hence the separate credit disclosure above. On the widest discount the bear is Rp117 before the haircut, and the same 10% haircut takes it below today's price of Rp150: no cushion. Probabilities are the house default because we have no information that shifts them.

**Signposts.** Watch the allowance as a share of net receivables against the audited level [S2]; the spread between the receivables yield and the finance charges line, which is the net interest margin in all but name [S3]; the rental book's revenue growth against the first half's rate; and the register — any raise, buyback or change in the parent's stake would move the discount far more than a quarter of earnings [S8].

Control is concentrated even by Indonesian standards. The listed parent holds the overwhelming majority, the ultimate parent is Gallant Venture Ltd, and the float is a small fraction [S3], [S8], [S0]. Minority holders have no influence over capital allocation, and the history shows capital allocation being used: four pre-emptive rights issues, the last completed in December 2025 with the proceeds paid as fresh equity into the rental subsidiary [S3]. We regard the serial use of rights issues at prices above the subsequent market as the single most important governance fact about this name. In the base case the share count is nonetheless flat: no raise is announced, and the audited cash flow funds the book with borrowings and bonds [S3], [S5].

Two further facts belong in the record, one dated. The exchange requires issuers below the large-cap threshold to lift their float to a minimum of 15.0% by 31 March 2029, and IMJS reports 8.0%, derived from the reported 92.0% parent stake [S10], [S8], [S0]. That is a regulatory clock on the register and belongs in the discount and the bear. The auditor is a member firm of a major network with an unmodified opinion whose key audit matters are the loan-loss allowance and the presentation of consumer financing receivables — the main reason we anchor value on the statement values [S3].

The board is conventional, with several commissioners, a single independent commissioner and an audit committee drawn from them [S3]. Related-party purchases, sales, receivables and payables are disclosed across both segments [S3]. The dividend is honest but thin: a token cash dividend for consecutive years, most recently 3.8 IDR bn, a fraction of a per cent on the price [S8], [S0]. Environmental and social exposure is low-intensity — fleet emissions standards and responsible-lending obligations, neither quantified in a way we can model [S3].

The near-term calendar is thin, which is itself informative: no announced corporate action would force the discount to narrow, and that absence is the hardest part of the call. The one dated corporate event is regulatory — the free-float deadline of 31 March 2029, obliging the group to lift the float from 8.0% to the minimum 15.0%, which can only be met by a controller sell-down or new shares [S10]. The other dated items are the third-quarter interim report, due by the end of this month and the first hard test of the recovery [S2]; the annual report and general meeting for the current financial year [S8]; and whatever the newly formed financing and venture-capital subsidiary does with its capital [S7].

Between updates we monitor four things: the allowance for impairment as a share of net financing receivables, the auditor's key judgement [S2]; the receivables yield against the finance charges line, the net interest margin in all but name [S3]; rental revenue against the fleet's net book value [S3]; and the register — the parent's stake, the float, and any proposed new shares [S8].

base.narrative: Revenue compounds from the first half's run rate, the financing book grows with the vehicle-market recovery, and the shares keep the wide discount the register and the governance record warrant: no narrowing is credited, because nothing in the calendar forces one.

bear.narrative: The vehicle-market recovery stalls, credit costs rise in the financing book (the auditor's key judgement) and the register stays shut, so the shares keep the widest discount of their own four observable years and the operating margin absorbs the receivable book's loss content.

bull.narrative: The recovery runs a second year, the rental fleet's utilisation lifts the margin, the new financing and venture arm earns its cost of capital and the family group upstreams cash, so the discount narrows within its own four observable years.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: The first half's own run rate carried into a weaker second half, then a step down to the deck's nominal path: the house macro deck compounds real output and prices in the mid single digits in the long run, and the long-run input holds that nominal path for a rental fleet and a financing book [S2], [S9]. The intermediate years decelerate as the vehicle-market recovery normalises.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at 38%, the level both segments delivered in the audited year and in the first half of 2026; the financing book's margin is set by the OJK rate environment and the rental book's by utilisation.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Net of other operating income: the filing's selling, G&A and other operating lines net to 21.2% of FY2025 revenue and 20.1% in 1H2026, so we hold ~20.5% rather than the data pack's narrower line.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: fleet depreciation at the audited rate: 15.8% of FY2025 revenue, 16.4% in 1H2026

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Fleet replacement and expansion: the audited cash-flow charge was 41.8% of FY2025 revenue and 37.2% in 1H2026; held at 40% for a rental book that must keep buying vehicles to grow revenue.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: the pack treats the financing book as operating working capital; held at the FY2025 ratio

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The first half's effective charge: 42.4% of pre-tax profit including the final tax, against 87.5% in FY2025 when profit before tax was thin and the final tax dominated.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: A blended all-in rate, not a full repricing. The held stock of Rp26,569.504bn is priced at the realised 3.31% (FY2025 finance charges of Rp880.181bn over that closing stock; the first half annualises to 3.26% on the same base) [S3], [S2]. The 7.8% marginal rate is the red team's accepted assumption from C11/C14, not a rate the filings disclose: S3 shows the syndicated facility sizes (F54, F60) and the fixed-rate bond programme but no coupon, so the 7.8% is labelled a red-team assumption rather than a sourced market price [S3]. With Rp2,900bn raised in FY2026 and charged for half a year, interest is 3.31% x opening debt plus 7.8% x half the new money, which is 3.74% of opening debt; the engine carries one scalar, so we hold that blended rate and disclose that it anchors FY2026 to the last actual while understating the marginal charge as new vintages accumulate in the later years of the explicit forecast. The audited 3.26-3.71% blended ratio is not a full-repricing warrant: it measures the without-recourse joint financing presented net, so the existing stock is held at its realised rate and only incremental money pays the assumed marginal price.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The financing book and the fleet are debt-funded: FY2025 debt rose Rp2,854.6bn net while receivables grew 18% [S3], so we fund the forecast working-capital and capex build at that rate, rising with the book.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Share of associates' net income, held at the audited run rate (Rp29.8bn in FY2025) as the associates are stable financing and logistics stakes.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Nil, the accepted NCI-at-nil basis of C12: the minority claim is being consumed, falling from Rp175.594bn at FY2024 to Rp91.853bn at FY2025 and Rp43.254bn at 30 June 2026 (F59, F64, F24), and the half-year allocation was again a loss of Rp49.747bn (F72); at that burn the balance is exhausted inside the forecast year, after which the group bears the loss in full and the minority allocation is nil. Setting the forecast allocation to nil also keeps the model on one basis with the earnings leg, which is now struck on the audited group result (F44); the earlier negative ratio has been removed because multiplying it by a positive group result produced a profit allocation to NCI, the sign error C15 identifies [S3], [S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The stated dividend record, not a policy ratio: the board has declared the same Rp0.35 per share for two consecutive years, so each year's payout percentage is exactly that fixed Rp0.35 distribution over the year's group earnings, which is why the ratio falls as earnings recover and why DPS is Rp0.35 in every forecast year and not nil (F30, S8). The percentages are re-struck on the group earnings the model now carries so that the Rp0.35 distribution is actually paid in every year rather than being suppressed by a negative or too-low earnings line.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No further capital action in the base case: no raise is announced in the registry and the audited cash-flow statement funds the fleet and the receivable book with bank borrowings and bonds rather than equity [S3], [S5]. The serial rights record - four pre-emptive issues, the last completed in December 2025 - is real and is carried where it belongs in this valuation, in the warranted holding-company discount, rather than as a share-count forecast we cannot date.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set on the deck's long-run nominal path for the rupiah economy rather than on the company's own recent growth: the fleet and the regulated financing book compound with nominal output, and the house rupiah cap keeps us below it.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: A governance and upstream discount only, benchmarked to the house card and to the name rather than a mark on the loan book: the finance book is now marked at its own disclosed Level 2 fair value (F65) and the fleet and other parts at carrying value, so the 60% does not double-count credit risk [S3]. The house base-rate card puts persistent holdco discounts at 20-40%, and the shares' own four observable years put the discount at roughly 41% to 70% (price to book 0.585x to 0.30x), so 60% is the wide end of the name's own range and above the house band [S0]. That is warranted by governance, not by a hoped-for re-rating: a 92% controller, four pre-emptive rights issues with the last paid at a price above the subsequent market, a token dividend, a float of 8.03% derived from the reported 91.97% parent stake (F31, S8) and carried in the data pack at that level [S0], and a regulatory obligation to lift that float to 15% by 31 March 2029 (F74, S10) that can only be met by a controller sell-down or new shares. With no dated narrowing catalyst we hold the wide end; the unmet catalyst is why the name is not a BUY.

challenges.challenge: Prior C3 was accepted on the group basis (F44 Rp19.175bn) with NCI at nil; the current model pe.metric is 122.855 (FY2025A parent, F47), so C3 is reversed, not implemented. On the group basis the P/E leg is 26.73 (15.122018 x 19.175 / 10,849.2625m shares), the blend 126.38 and the twelve-month target 137.91 against the 150 price, so the ADD fails. §4's 'one earnings basis' paragraph argues parent is the right basis, but the model's own forecast now has parent losses of -1,138.57 (FY2026E) to -2,027.48 (FY2035E), so the leg capitalises a positive FY2025A profit the forecast says never recurs. The basis choice is dispositive (184 vs 138), and the prior accepted correction is not in the files.
challenges.answer: Implemented in the model, not reconciled in prose. The FY2023-FY2025 earnings history is now keyed to the audited group totals (F44 Rp19.175bn, F66 Rp130.301bn, F67 Rp269.601bn), the forecast allocates nil to minorities, and the P/E metric the engine binds is the audited group result 19.175, not the parent 122.855. The leg is now Rp26.73 at 15.122x, against the SOTP's Rp159.73; the blend is Rp126.48, the twelve-month target Rp137.69 and the total return -8.0%, so the rating moves from ADD to HOLD [S3], [S0], [F44], [F66], [F67]. The forecast parent path is no longer negative: the split-rate funding fix (C14) and the nil minority allocation produce a positive group/parent path from Rp167.35bn to Rp489.64bn, so the leg no longer capitalises a profit the forecast says never recurs. The anchor year is stated in section four: the audited group year is the committed anchor and the LTM group bridge is disclosed as the upside cross-check, which still does not restore the ADD after the liquidity haircut.

challenges.challenge: C11's 7.8% is in the model, but it is applied to the whole opening debt stock (DEBT[-1] x a.cost_of_debt), not just new money: FY2026E interest is 2,072.42 against FY2025A 880.181 (2.35x) because the existing Rp24.5tn is repriced overnight. The result is group losses in every forecast year (-790.18 FY2026E to -1,747.23 FY2035E) and parent losses (-1,138.57 to -2,027.48), against 1H2026A parent profit +169.944 (F26). That is not the most-likely base case, it is not disclosed, and §3's line that 'the turn in the operating line and the cash flow is what would lift that leg first' points the other way. It also forces dps 0.00, contradicting the Rp0.35 prose.
challenges.answer: Implemented as a split rate. The held stock of Rp26,569.504bn is priced at its realised 3.31% (FY2025 finance charges of Rp880.181bn over that closing stock; the first half annualises to 3.26%), and only the Rp2,900bn of FY2026 net new borrowing pays the accepted 7.8% marginal rate, charged for half a year; the engine carries one scalar, so the blended all-in input is 3.74% on opening debt [S3], [S2], [F5], [F54], [F60]. The interest path is now Rp993.7bn in FY2026 rising to Rp2,127.8bn by FY2035, against Rp880.2bn audited — FY2026 is the last actual plus half a year of new money, not an overnight repricing of the whole book. PBT and np are positive in every forecast year (group np Rp167.4bn in FY2026, Rp489.6bn by FY2035) and the FY2026 group result is above the 1H2026A group result of Rp120.197bn; the H2 step-down from the H1 annualised pace is the half-year charge on the new debt, and the first half's own debt growth was held down by the December rights-issue proceeds paid into the rental subsidiary (F32), so the base case no longer contradicts the interim. The later years understate the marginal charge as new vintages accumulate because the scalar cannot be vintage-specific, and section three discloses that rather than smoothing it.

challenges.challenge: C12's forward NCI is implemented with a sign/magnitude error. minority_pct -0.4409 times FY2026E np -790.18 produces a +348.39 minority allocation (a profit to NCI; model.lines.minority), while the stated basis is 'about Rp100bn a year of losses' (-98.176 FY2024A, -103.680 FY2025A, -49.747 1H2026). As a result np_parent -1,138.57 is worse than group np -790.18 - the parent absorbs more than 100% of the loss, the opposite of a minority absorbing losses. The prior C12 accepted response said NCI-at-nil, so neither the accepted nor the stated alternative is actually met.
challenges.answer: Fixed. minority_pct is set to nil in every forecast year, the accepted C12 NCI-at-nil basis, so the sign-inverted ratio that turned a group loss into a +Rp348.39bn allocation to NCI is gone and np equals np_parent in the forecast [S3], [S2]. The basis is sourced to the consuming minority balance (F59 Rp175.594bn at FY2024, F64 Rp91.853bn at FY2025, F24 Rp43.254bn at 30 June 2026) and the half-year allocation of -Rp49.747bn (F72): at that burn the claim is exhausted inside the forecast year, after which the group bears the loss in full. The parent/group split is shown from the audited facts: group Rp19.175bn (F44), parent Rp122.855bn (F47), NCI -Rp103.680bn (F46) for FY2025, and group Rp120.197bn / parent Rp169.944bn / NCI -Rp49.747bn for 1H2026 (F72, F26). This is the reversal of the prior modelled-forward treatment, recorded here and in section three.

challenges.challenge: The card says a holdco discount is the base rate and a discount-narrowing thesis needs a named, dated catalyst; with none, route to EVENT_SPECIAL_SIT or pass. The report says 'we have none to name' but rates ADD. The entire 22.9% expected return is the roll-forward: v0 168.885 x (1 + COE 0.2124) = 204.76, x (1 - 0.10) = 184.29; without the COE roll the same marks give 152.0 against the 150 price. No evidence is offered that a carrying-value book compounds at 21.2% when the audited ROE is 0.38% (F48).
challenges.answer: No discount-narrowing catalyst can be named and dated, so the card's route is taken and the rating is downgraded rather than left at ADD: the total return of -8.0% lands in HOLD [S0], [S3]. Section four now states plainly that the expected return is the mechanical cost-of-equity roll on static marks, not a view that the discount narrows, and it publishes the static-mark value (Rp126.48 before the roll and liquidity haircut) alongside the target. The one dated corporate event, the 31 March 2029 free-float deadline, is a supply event that widens rather than narrows the discount, and it is disclosed in sections five, six and seven (F74, S10). The earlier claim that the ADD rested on the discount while all of its return came from the roll is therefore removed, not reworded.

challenges.challenge: The two risks the report ranks highest - credit cost in the financing book (the auditor's KAM) and refinancing - are not in the scenario values. The bear only adds 10pp to holdco_discount and -3pp to revenue growth; both leave the SOTP marks (16,664.372 financing receivables, F39) and the FY2025A P/E metric unchanged. The report says a mark haircut is not expressible, but a gross_margin or opex_pct shock is (the prior round used a margin shock). The bear 168.84 is pre-liquidity; after the same 10% haircut it is 151.95, barely above the 150 price, so the 'still above the market' cushion is a presentation artefact.
challenges.answer: Accepted on all three parts. The bear and bull now carry a mirrored gross-margin shock of plus or minus two points in addition to the discount and revenue shocks, which is the operating channel through which credit cost reaches the forecast; the scenarios table shows the pre-haircut values and section five publishes the bear after the same house liquidity haircut, which puts it below today's price rather than above it [S2], [S3]. The credit content of the finance mark is disclosed separately: the book is marked at its disclosed fair value of Rp15,995.100bn against a carrying value of Rp16,664.372bn (F65, F39), the non-current allowance is Rp426.012bn (F76), and a further deterioration has to exhaust both the mark already taken and that allowance before it reaches our value. The engine's shock grammar cannot re-mark a holding, so the mark channel is disclosed in prose and the operating channel is in the scenario, with the limitation stated rather than hidden.

challenges.challenge: The model registry (valuation.konglo.profile.free_float) shows free_float_pct 8.03 against min_pct 15.0, gap 6.97pp, compliant false, next_step_by 2029-03-31. The report discloses the 8.03% in the liquidity paragraph but never the 15% minimum or the 2029 deadline, and states 'no raise is announced in the registry' and 'no dated corporate action'. A regulatory deadline to lift the float by 6.97pp is a dated supply/dilution event, and the four-rights- issue record (LPO IV, S3 p13) makes a placement plausible. It belongs in the bear and in the discount rationale.
challenges.answer: Disclosed and sourced. The exchange requires issuers below the large-cap threshold to reach a minimum free float of 15% by 31 March 2029 (F74, S10), and IMJS reports 8.03% [S0]. The report now names the deadline in sections five, six and seven and in the frontmatter catalyst list, discusses the only two routes that can close the gap (a controller sell-down or new shares, with the four-issue rights record making a placement plausible), and carries the overhang in the governance discount. The 'no dated corporate action' claim is reconciled by narrowing it to 'no announced corporate action': the regulatory deadline is the one dated event on the calendar, and it widens rather than narrows the discount.

challenges.challenge: The P/E leg uses the FY2025A parent trough 122.855 even though LTM parent is 193.34 (F26 169.944 + F47 122.855 - 1H2025 99.459, S2 p8) and 1H2026A alone is 169.944. C3's own parent option (LTM 193.34) gives 269.48/share at the same 15.122x multiple versus 171.24 now, so the report understates the earnings recovery it describes in §3. The justification - 'the weakest audited year corroborates the marks' - is a conservatism choice with no most-likely source.
challenges.answer: The LTM bridge is now published in section four, on the group basis the accepted correction requires: the audited group result (F44) plus the current first half (F72) less the prior-year first half (F71) gives the LTM group result, and the report states that putting the same multiple on it would lift the leg to several times the audited-year value and put the static blend at about today's price [S3], [S2]. Even that most generous group anchor leaves the target a HOLD after the liquidity haircut, so the direction of the call does not depend on the choice. The LTM parent figure (F47 plus F26 less F73) is not used: the parent line flatters the economics by pushing the sub-entities' losses onto a minority claim that is being consumed, and putting it on the leg would re-create the basis the FATAL C3/C13 correction removed [S3]. The audited group year is therefore the committed anchor, with the LTM group bridge disclosed as the upside cross-check rather than carried.

challenges.challenge: The SOTP marks the financing book at 1.0x its carrying value (F39 16,664.372, 57.2% of the 29,138.038 gross parts) while the same report zeroes the P/BV leg because a book earning 0.38% ROE against 21.2% COE supports a negative justified P/B. The 60% holdco discount cannot simultaneously be a governance discount and the impairment of a loan book; the card separates the two. The report also calls the amortised-cost loan marks a 'floor', which is backwards for receivables: carrying value is an upper bound if credit losses exceed the 426.012 allowance (S3 p271).
challenges.answer: The finance book is now marked at its own disclosed Level 2 fair value of Rp15,995.100bn (F65, S3) instead of its Rp16,664.372bn carrying value (F39): the notes value the book by discounting cash flows at the weighted-average effective interest rate, so the mark is a sourced credit-and-rate view, not a blanket multiple. That separates the credit impairment from the holding-company discount, and the 60% discount is now stated as a governance and upstream discount only, benchmarked to the house 20-40% base-rate card and the name's own four observable price-to-book years [S0]. The 'floor' language is removed from the investment summary and section four; the report now states that the matched interim re-mark lowers net asset value (C22). The negative justified P/B continues to remove the P/BV leg, but it no longer doubles as an argument about the receivables mark.

challenges.challenge: The SOTP omits the group's other net assets. Marked parts are 29,138.038; total assets 32,901.634 (F23) less marked parts less cash 2,077.414 (F21) leaves 1,686.182 of other assets; total liabilities 27,808.191 (F22) less debt 26,569.504 (F63) leaves 1,238.687 of other liabilities; net 447.495. That is exactly the gap between SOTP NAV 4,554.095 and parent book equity 5,001.590 (F49), so 447.5bn of net assets is dropped without explanation. At the same discount and roll it is worth about 18/share (447.495 x 0.4 / 10,849.2625m x 1.2124 x 0.9).
challenges.answer: The residual net assets are now in the sum of the parts as a sourced holding: total assets of Rp32,901.634bn (F23) less the four marked balances and cash of Rp2,077.414bn (F21) leaves the non-marked assets, total liabilities of Rp27,808.191bn (F22) less interest-bearing debt of Rp26,569.504bn (F63) leaves the non-debt liabilities, and their net of Rp447.495bn is carried [S3]. The bridge then reconciles: the marked parts plus the residual less look-through net debt and the minority claim equal parent book equity of Rp5,001.590bn (F49) before the fair-value mark, and the fair-value mark on the finance book (F65 vs F39) is the last step to NAV. The report table and the section-four bridge show each line, so nothing is dropped and the NAV is traceable from total assets to the per-share value.

challenges.challenge: The post-balance-sheet paragraph calls the 31 Dec 2025 marks 'a floor on the interim sheet'. Using the report's own 30 June 2026 figures, the marked parts rise by 654.100 (F55-F38 457.906; F56-F19 8.530; F57-F20 30.496; F58-F40 157.168) but net debt rises by 905.075 (25,397.165 vs 24,492.090) and NCI falls by 48.599 (43.254 vs 91.853); the matched re-mark lowers NAV by 202.376 to 4,351.719. The audited marks are a peak, not a floor, in net terms, and the sentence flatters the value.
challenges.answer: The 'floor' claim is removed from the investment summary, section four and the post-balance-sheet note. The report now states the matched net effect: at 30 June 2026 the marked parts are higher (fleet F55, investment property F56, investment in shares F57, non-current receivables F58) but so are the matching liabilities, with total interest-bearing debt at Rp26,948.708bn against Rp26,569.504bn (F68 vs F63), cash at Rp1,551.543bn against Rp2,077.414bn (F69 vs F21) and the minority claim at Rp43.254bn against Rp91.853bn (F24 vs F64), so the matched re-mark lowers net asset value by Rp202.376bn — from Rp4,332.318bn to Rp4,129.942bn on our fair-value-marked NAV — rather than raising it [S2], [S3]. The audited marks are therefore a peak in net terms, not a floor.

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter thesis says '{{val.methods.pe.multiple}} times book own-history multiple', which renders as 15.12 times book; 15.12 is the P/E multiple, while the own-history P/BV is 0.585x (model own_history.pbv, n=4). The model's pe.basis also still reads 'own five-year average' although own_history n=4, the labelling C3 asked to fix.
challenges.answer: The erroneous '15.12 times book' claim is removed from the frontmatter thesis; the thesis no longer attaches a multiple to the book leg and states that the own-history book multiple has no supportable value at an audited ROE of 0.38% against a cost of equity above twenty per cent [S0], [S3], [F48]. The report labels the price-to-earnings multiple as the mean of four observable observations everywhere it is described. The model output's pe.basis string still reads 'own five-year average' because that label is a hard-coded constant in the engine's target_multiple() and the instruction is not to edit scripts; the computation behind it uses n=4, and the report says so. The basis label is therefore correct in the report and cosmetic in the model, which we record rather than paper over.

challenges.challenge: §6 says 'the filing records the December 2025 exchange suspension over the cumulative price rise' [S3]. Grep of S3 (386 pages) and S5 for suspension/penghentian/halt returns no hit; the claim is not verifiable in the cited source. It is one of the governance facts supporting the 60% discount.
challenges.answer: Deleted. The red team is right that the claim is not in S3 or S5, and no registered source contains an exchange suspension announcement, so the sentence is removed from section five and section six rather than re-cited. The liquidity and governance sections no longer rely on it; the thinness of the register is evidenced by the reported float and the traded value [S0], and the dated supply event that remains is the free-float deadline (F74, S10).

challenges.challenge: qc reports a 1.41pp calibration gap (FY2025A EBITDA margin 0.3259 vs FY2026E 0.34) with no qc_justification, and the model pays dps 0.00 in every forecast year (model.lines.dps FY2026E-FY2035E) while §3 says 'the recorded per-share distribution is what every forecast year pays' and the payout basis says 'DPS is Rp0.35 in every forecast year and not nil'. The report and model disagree on the dividend.
challenges.answer: Both fixed. The dividend is restored in the model: the payout percentages are re-struck on the group earnings the model now carries so dps is Rp0.35 in every forecast year (FY2026-FY2035), matching the audited record and the section-three prose [S8], [F30]. The calibration gap now has a sourced justification in qc_justifications: the FY2026E EBITDA margin sits above the audited year because the first half delivered it, with gross profit of Rp1,265.584bn on revenue of Rp3,310.678bn (38.2%) against 37.9% for FY2025 and operating income plus depreciation of Rp600.150bn and Rp541.129bn (34.5%) against 32.6% [S2], [S3], [F75]. The 1.41pp gap sits inside the engine's 5pp calibration band, so the flag does not fire and the justification is recorded as an orphan; we say so rather than pretend a BLOCK was cleared.

missing_bull_case.note: Two sourced upsides are absent from value. The P/E leg uses the FY2025A parent trough 122.855 (F47) although LTM parent is 193.34 (F26 169.944 + F47 122.855 - 1H2025 99.459, S2 p8) and C3's own parent option gives 269.48/share, not 171.24. And the SOTP omits the group's net other assets: 32,901.634 (F23) less marked parts 29,138.038 less cash 2,077.414 (F21) = 1,686.182 assets, against 27,808.191 (F22) less debt 26,569.504 (F63) = 1,238.687 liabilities, i.e. 447.495bn dropped, exactly the gap between SOTP NAV 4,554.095 and parent book equity 5,001.590 (F49).

missing_bear_case.note: The two risks the report itself ranks highest - credit cost in the financing book (the auditor's KAM) and refinancing - never reach the scenario values: the bear only adds 10pp to holdco_discount and -3pp to revenue growth, neither of which touches the 16,664.372 receivable mark (F39) or the FY2025A P/E metric. The report says a mark haircut is not expressible, yet a gross_margin/opex shock is (the prior round used one). It also omits the 8.03%-vs-15% free-float gap due 2029-03-31 in the model registry, and quotes the bear at 168.84 pre-liquidity while the headline target is post-liquidity (151.95).

assumption_realism.note: cost_of_debt 7.8% (inputs.cost_of_debt 0.078) is applied to the whole opening debt stock (DEBT[-1] x a.cost_of_debt), not just new money: FY2026E interest 2,072.42 against FY2025A 880.181 (2.35x), producing group losses every year (-790.18 FY2026E to -1,747.23 FY2035E) and parent losses (-1,138.57 to -2,027.48) against 1H2026A parent profit +169.944 (F26). Separately minority_pct -0.4409 multiplied by negative np yields a +348.39 allocation to NCI (model.lines.minority), the opposite of the stated ~100bn of NCI losses (-98.176 FY2024A, -103.680 FY2025A, -49.747 1H2026). Neither drift is reconciled to the last actual or the interim.

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checks verified: F44/F47/NCI -103.680 (S3 p66), F48 ROE 0.38% (S3 p8), F39 16,664.372 (S3 p271), F30 Rp0.35/Rp3.8bn/3.1% (S8), F24 43.254 and F26 169.944/-49.747/120.197 (S2 p6/p8), LPO IV (S3 p13). But the December 2025 exchange suspension claimed in §6 is not found in S3 (386 pages) or S5 by grep for suspension/penghentian/halt; the 15%/2029 free-float rule is in the model registry but absent from the report; and the frontmatter calls 15.12x the 'book' multiple when own-history P/BV is 0.585x (model own_history.pbv).

valuation_method_fit.note: SOTP is the right primary, but it is applied outside the card's discipline. No named and dated discount catalyst, which the card says routes the idea to EVENT_SPECIAL_SIT or pass, yet the rating is ADD. The finance book is marked at 1.0x book (F39, 57.2% of the 29,138.038 gross parts) after the P/BV leg was zeroed for a negative justified P/B. 447.495bn of net other assets is dropped. And the 22.9% expected return is the COE roll on a static carrying value (v0 168.885 x 1.2124 x 0.9 = 184.29), not a view on the discount, which the card requires.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says the discount is held and no narrowing is credited, while the entire 22.9% comes from rolling a static book mark at COE 21.24% (without the roll the marks give 152.0 against the 150 price). It calls amortised-cost loan receivables a 'floor' although a matched 30 June 2026 re-mark lowers NAV by 202.376bn (assets +654.100, net debt +905.075, NCI benefit +48.599). And it compares the pre-liquidity bear 168.84 to the price while the headline 184 is post-liquidity.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the macro deck correctly (BI 5.75%, USDIDR 18,350, AVOID tilt on rate-sensitive consumer names acknowledged in §2) and uses the CONGLOMERATES SOTP template. But the 60% holdco discount sits outside the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT 20-40% band and is not benchmarked against the sector deck's base-rate card or the CONGLOMERATES comps, and the own-history discount range is four years, not the card's five. The 7.8% forecast cost of debt is also below the engine's own kd_pre_tax 9.45% in the cost-of-capital block.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative: P/E on the FY2025A trough (122.855 vs LTM 193.34), SOTP drops 447.495bn of net other assets, and the bull discount stops at 50% although the own-history top is 41%. Optimistic: the financing book is marked at 1.0x book despite a 0.38% ROE against 21.2% COE, and the 'floor' language on loan marks. The stack moves the target by roughly 9-18% in either direction, so it is not a rounding difference.

calibration.note: qc shows no blocking flags, but FY2026E EBITDA margin 0.34 against FY2025A 0.3259 is a 1.41pp gap with no qc_justification, and the model pays dps 0.00 in every forecast year (model.lines.dps FY2026E-FY2035E) while §3 says the Rp0.35 is paid every forecast year and the payout basis says 'not nil'. The report and model disagree on the dividend.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. HOLD, target Rp138 (-8.0%) reproduces from the model: SOTP Rp160 (75%) and P/E Rp26.7 (25%) blend to Rp126.5 today, rolled at the 21.2% cost of equity and cut by the 10% ADTV haircut to Rp138. Both anchors are HOLD: the report's LTM bridge (F44 Rp19.2bn + F72 Rp120.0bn - F71 Rp49.8bn = Rp89.6bn) at the same 15.1x gives a Rp125/share leg, a Rp151 static blend and about Rp165 after the roll and haircut, the top of the HOLD band. QC's too_bearish finding is accepted and correctly attributed to a capability gap, not the analyst: the engine binds the P/E metric to the last restated history line and exposes no LTM hook, so the published target is the audited-trough floor. Recorded as a desk/Director capability FIX: add a sourced LTM metric basis (valuation.pe.metric or an LTM fact the multiple leg can read) before the next version; do not restate an audited year or touch the pack to emulate it. Section 4 publishes the bridge, its components and the floor label, which is sufficient disclosure for this version. Most-likely check: scenarios are mirrored (holdco discount +/-0.10, revenue +/-3pp, gross margin +/-2pp; 25/50/25, base 50%); the only base-case haircuts are the 60% governance discount (wide end of the name's own 41-70% band, inside the 62% market-implied) and the ADTV rule, each sourced; no shared-input tilt, and the CONGLOMERATES batch is mixed (BUY/ADD/HOLD/REDUCE/SELL). The 60% discount matches ABMM's only coincidentally, on this name's own four-year band and 92% control. Not konglo per the registry (HSC false); the 8.03% float and the 31 March 2029 deadline are carried as dated risk, not a lens, which is correct. No covered Indomobil sibling; no model contamination found. Prose for the next version: state that the published call moves from ADD (Rp184) to HOLD (Rp138); the body omits the rating change. Q3 length and the Q6 comma splice clear next version.

bias.note: The published target of Rp138 is struck on the FY2025A group trough because the engine binds the P/E metric to the last restated history line (Rp19.175bn, F44), giving a leg of Rp26.73, although the report's own LTM group result is Rp89.575bn (F44 + F72 - F71, [S2], [S3]) and at the same 15.12x gives about Rp124.9/share; the static blend would be about Rp151 and the rolled, haircut target about Rp165 (+9.9%), not Rp138 (-8.0%). The analyst concedes in Q1 and section 4 that the LTM is the more likely earnings level and labels Rp138 the floor of the range. The own-history P/E multiple is itself derived on parent earnings (FY2025A 24.90x = Rp282 x 10.849bn shares / Rp122.855bn parent, datapack history_multiples) and is applied to the group result, a second conservative layer disclosed in section 4 ('struck on parent earnings'). Every other conservative choice is sourced or house law: the 60% discount is the wide end of the name's own 41-70% range and inside the market-implied 62%; the 10% haircut is the ADTV rule at Rp0.93bn; the finance book is at its disclosed Level 2 fair value; no discount narrowing without a dated catalyst; NCI nil on an exhausted claim. The optimistic offsets (21.2% cost-of-equity roll, 18% FY2026E revenue growth, nil NCI on recovering profits) are disclosed. The defect is the trough anchor, not the HOLD, and both anchors are HOLD.

recomputed.item: FY2025A financing receivables at disclosed fair value
LTM group net profit (F44+F72-F71) carried in the P/E leg

findings.finding: The analyst's Q1 answer is honest and its structural claim is verified in the engine, not just asserted: fund record m_multiple strikes the P/E leg on mkt['ltm']['np_parent'], and market() overwrites that LTM figure with the last restated history line whenever np_parent is restated (fund record:493-499). With F44 (Rp19.175bn) restated, the leg cannot be struck on the LTM from any allowed input: the only valuation hooks read from assumptions are bridge, weights, multiple_source, peers, coe_premium, roe_sustainable and holdco_net_debt (no metric override); fund record and scripts are off-limits; and fund record rejects typed numbers, so Rp124.9 and Rp165 cannot be printed directly. The report publishes the LTM bridge and its consequence in section 4 (F44 + F72 - F71 = Rp89.575bn; about Rp124.9/share at 15.12x; blend about Rp151; target at the top of the HOLD band) and labels Rp138 the floor. The leg, and therefore the target, remains materially below the report's own more-likely anchor; the analyst could not have fixed it within the allowed inputs, so this is a capability gap, not an analyst defect.
findings.answer: The LTM group basis is now published in section four, not summarised: its components (the audited group total F44 plus the current first half F72 less the prior-year first half F71), the same own-history multiple applied to them, and the consequence — the static blend reaches about the price and the twelve-month target sits at the top of the HOLD band, still HOLD. The published target remains on the audited group year, and section four now states plainly why rather than defending the trough as most likely: the engine binds the earnings leg to the last audited actual in the model's history, so striking it on the LTM group result would require either restating an audited year in fund record (which would be a false fact) or editing the data pack (forbidden to the analyst). I cannot source a reason the trough is the most probable anchor, because there is none; the honest position is that the LTM is the more likely earnings level and the audited year is what the model binds. Both give HOLD, so the call does not turn on the choice, and the published target is labelled in section four as the floor of the range rather than a point estimate. Escalated to the Sector Lead: the P/E leg needs an LTM-basis capability the analyst cannot create under the current engine [S3], [S2], [S0].

The own-history P/E multiple (mean 15.12x) is computed on parent earnings in the data pack (history_multiples FY2025A 24.90x equals Rp282 x 10.849bn shares / Rp122.855bn parent; on the group total it would have been about 159x and excluded by the cap), while section 4 applies it to the group result. That scope mismatch understates the leg further than the NCI-at-nil forward basis implies. It is disclosed ("struck on parent earnings"), which is why this is a note rather than a block.
